​Urgent news: GPT-6 Astra has just passed ALL 48 levels of the "I am not a robot" CAPTCHA.

OpenAI engineer Sharif Shamim watched as Astra navigated through all the existing CAPTCHA challenges, which range from simple image recognition to parking, chess, puzzles, and interactive UI challenges.

Astra completed all tasks designed to distinguish between humans and bots, utilizing its computer abilities to understand what is happening on the screen and directly perform actions.

If you have not yet realized what has happened, the world has become less secure from today onwards. Any user of GPT-6 Astra can now crack any existing CAPTCHA in the world. This means they can write any exploits to bypass CAPTCHA and launch attacks on any websites.

Credit must be given to security engineers; figuratively speaking, they are not sleeping and are continuously working to enhance security measures.

As traditional CAPTCHAs (ReCAPTCHA v2, hCaptcha) are increasingly being hacked by automation, the industry is shifting towards behavioral analysis (e.g., ReCAPTCHA v3 or Cloudflare Turnstile).

These methods work seamlessly for users, analyzing mouse movements, browser history, IP address, and other parameters to differentiate between humans and bots without the need to click on images.

However, as you may have already understood, all these tactics will not stop GPT-6 Astra, as it is constantly active, decoding every trick faster than they can be devised.

The initial models of Chat GPT were ridiculed by cybersecurity experts, claiming things like: "Your AI won't even be able to pass a CAPTCHA, what kind of intelligence is that?" But with the emergence of GPT-6 Astra, cybersecurity professionals are no longer laughing.

Moreover, not only can the new AI models crack any CAPTCHA, but they now prevent the creation of anything new that could stay functional for even a couple of hours.

Now that Astra is available not only to cybersecurity companies and white hats but also to nefarious actors, including the Lazarus Group (a well-known state-sponsored hacking group operating for North Korea's intelligence services), the situation is concerning.

When Klaus Schwab predicted to us a "massive cyberattack" followed by a blackout, it was funny. Now, not so much.

📌 DeFi Interest Models: Why Borrow Rates Keep Changing

Main Points
⏺ DeFi borrow rates often depend on demand and pool utilization
⏺ The more liquidity is borrowed, the more expensive new loans become
⏺ This post explains why lending rates aren’t fixed like a bank quote

1️⃣ Core Idea — a lending protocol adjusts rates through a formula, not a human manager.
2️⃣ Pool Utilization — when most assets are borrowed, rates rise to attract liquidity and reduce demand.
3️⃣ Low Utilization — when supply is high and borrowing is low, rates usually drop.
4️⃣ Risk Surface — sudden borrowing demand can quickly raise your position cost and break a strategy.
5️⃣ Practical Rule — check not only the current rate, but utilization, rate history, and available liquidity.

Final Thoughts

A DeFi rate is not a promise — it’s a live market reaction. A loan can look cheap today and become expensive tomorrow.

🔐 Compliance Data Leak Exposes 291 Crypto Users' Identities

A data leak has linked the real identities of 291 crypto users directly to their wallet activity, stripping away the anonymity they relied on.

Copied support records exposed varying combinations of personal identity, location, and compliance data. Private keys and customer funds were not compromised in the incident.

The breach highlights a persistent vulnerability in crypto: while blockchain transactions can be pseudonymous, KYC and compliance records held by centralized services create a paper trail that, if exposed, can permanently de-anonymize users.

📌 Bitcoin price stalls near $82K as key resistance holds 

🌐 Bitcoin price pulled back after briefly breaking above $82,000 on Sept. 4, as traders took profits following a short squeeze driven by softer Federal Reserve expectations and renewed demand for US spot Bitcoin ETFs. According to data from cryptonews, Bitcoin price traded near $81,150 at the time of writing, having failed to hold an intraday move above the $82,000 psychological level. The pullback left the asset about 1% below its local high but still well above the $80,000 mark reclaimed during the previous session. 

⚠️ The rally accelerated after Bitcoin moved out of a range around $77,000–$79,000. Short sellers were forced to close leveraged positions as the price crossed $80,000, adding automatic buy orders to the market. CoinGlass data cited by market reports showed that the broader crypto market recorded more than $500 million in liquidations during the rally, with short positions accounting for most of the total. Bitcoin shorts reportedly absorbed about $415 million of those losses.

📊 Price action has since slowed near a technically important area. Galaxy Research data shared by analyst Quinten François placed Bitcoin’s 50-week moving average near $81,041, almost level with the current market price. According to François, Bitcoin has not closed a weekly candle above that moving average since November 2025. He said a move through $82,800 would also produce the first higher high of the broader downtrend and bring $90,000 back into consideration.
